items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Dick' in the context of a namesake for 'du vin' and later asks 'Dick Allen?' in response to the interviewer, but provides no personal narrative or interaction details.

ctx.x: Yeah, du vin is wine. Repeat that a couple more times for Dick, please. That's his namesake. That's his namesake. The three words, huh? No, just the wine. Mo, boire, plenty, du vin. That's four words.
Are you saying du vin? Du vin, yeah. Wine and du vin.

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: The interviewee addresses the interviewer as 'Dick' ('You ain't never been that old folks home, Dick.') and the interviewer identifies himself as 'Dick Allen'. The interviewee does not describe a professional or personal relationship with Dick Allen beyond this interaction.

ctx.x: Yeah, but I mean, that band stayed the entire two years at the Rialto. Yeah. Rialto.

And then what happened? Then, uh, after I left the Rialto, I started with, you know, after I left the Rialto, I think I must have went to Lutches. What's Lutches? Bill Paul down there, old folks home. That's Lutches. Yeah. Yeah. What goes on there? You ain't never been that old folks home, Dick. No. You're a little chug. You can't tell me. I know Dick killed me. I know Dick killed me. I was a monster and beret. Yeah. Yeah. I stayed there, huh? No, but what was it then when you first went there? Same thing it is…

What was it before you went in? Oh, it was a restaurant and bar. Used to have seafood, you know, thing like that. And the bar and port. And, uh, where the dance division is now, that was open. That was open between there and the house in the back, which is the home. They lived there and they had empty light in between. They closed the lot and built a dance hall.
